solution:
As \(\sin\dfrac{\pi}{4} = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\) and \(0 \le \dfrac{\pi}{4} < 2\pi\), \(\dfrac{\pi}{4}\) is a principal solution.
By allied angle formula, \(\sin\theta = \sin(\pi - \theta)\).
\(\therefore \sin\dfrac{\pi}{4} = \sin\left(\pi - \dfrac{\pi}{4}\right) = \sin\dfrac{3\pi}{4}\) and \(0 \le \dfrac{3\pi}{4} < 2\pi\).
\(\therefore \dfrac{3\pi}{4}\) is also a principal solution.
\(\therefore \dfrac{\pi}{4}\) and \(\dfrac{3\pi}{4}\) are the principal solutions of \(\sin\theta = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\).

As \(\cos\dfrac{\pi}{3} = \dfrac{1}{2}\) and \(0 \le \dfrac{\pi}{3} < 2\pi\), \(\dfrac{\pi}{3}\) is a principal solution.
By allied angle formula, \(\cos\theta = \cos(2\pi - \theta)\).
\(\therefore \cos\dfrac{\pi}{3} = \cos\left(2\pi - \dfrac{\pi}{3}\right) = \cos\dfrac{5\pi}{3}\) and \(0 \le \dfrac{5\pi}{3} < 2\pi\).
\(\therefore \dfrac{5\pi}{3}\) is also a principal solution.
\(\therefore \dfrac{\pi}{3}\) and \(\dfrac{5\pi}{3}\) are the principal solutions of \(\cos\theta = \dfrac{1}{2}\).

We know that \(\cos\dfrac{\pi}{3} = \dfrac{1}{2}\).
As \(\cos(\pi - \theta) = \cos(\pi + \theta) = -\cos\theta\),
\(\cos\left(\pi - \dfrac{\pi}{3}\right) = -\cos\dfrac{\pi}{3} = -\dfrac{1}{2}\) and \(\cos\left(\pi + \dfrac{\pi}{3}\right) = -\cos\dfrac{\pi}{3} = -\dfrac{1}{2}\).
\(\therefore \cos\dfrac{2\pi}{3} = -\dfrac{1}{2}\) and \(\cos\dfrac{4\pi}{3} = -\dfrac{1}{2}\).
Also \(0 \le \dfrac{2\pi}{3} \le 2\pi\) and \(0 \le \dfrac{4\pi}{3} < 2\pi\). Therefore \(\dfrac{2\pi}{3}\) and \(\dfrac{4\pi}{3}\) are principal solutions of \(\cos\theta = -\dfrac{1}{2}\).

We know that \(\cot\theta = -\sqrt{3}\) if and only if \(\tan\theta = -\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\).
We know that \(\tan\dfrac{\pi}{6} = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\).
Using identities, \(\tan(\pi - \theta) = -\tan\theta\) and \(\tan(2\pi - \theta) = -\tan\theta\), we get
\(\tan\dfrac{5\pi}{6} = -\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\) and \(\tan\dfrac{11\pi}{6} = -\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\).
And \(0 \le \dfrac{5\pi}{6} < 2\pi\) and \(0 \le \dfrac{11\pi}{6} < 2\pi\).
\(\therefore \dfrac{5\pi}{6}\) and \(\dfrac{11\pi}{6}\) are required principal solutions.

stem: Find the Cartesian co-ordinates of the point whose polar co-ordinates are \(\left(2, \dfrac{\pi}{4}\right)\).
solution:
Given \(r = 2\) and \(\theta = \dfrac{\pi}{4}\).
Using \(x = r\cos\theta\) and \(y = r\sin\theta\), we get
\(x = 2\cos\dfrac{\pi}{4} = 2 \times \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}} = \sqrt{2}\) and \(y = 2\sin\dfrac{\pi}{4} = 2 \times \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}} = \sqrt{2}\).
The required Cartesian co-ordinates are \(\left(\sqrt{2}, \sqrt{2}\right)\).

stem: Find the polar co-ordinates of the point whose Cartesian co-ordinates are \(\left(\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}, \dfrac{-1}{\sqrt{2}}\right)\).
solution:
From the co-ordinates of the given point we observe that the point lies in the fourth quadrant.
\(r^2 = x^2 + y^2 = \left(\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\right)^2 + \left(-\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\right)^2 = \dfrac{1}{2} + \dfrac{1}{2} = 1\), so \(r = 1\).
Since \(x = r\cos\theta\) and \(y = r\sin\theta\), \(\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}} = 1 \times \cos\theta\) and \(-\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}} = 1 \times \sin\theta\).
Hence \(\cos\theta = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\) and \(\sin\theta = -\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\), so \(\theta = \dfrac{7\pi}{4}\).
The required polar co-ordinates are \(\left(1, \dfrac{7\pi}{4}\right)\).

subtopic: Solution of Triangle — Sine, Cosine and Projection Rules
stem: In \(\triangle ABC\), if \(A = 30^\circ\), \(B = 60^\circ\) then find the ratio of sides.
solution:
To find \(a : b : c\). Given \(A = 30^\circ\), \(B = 60^\circ\).
As \(A, B, C\) are angles of the triangle, \(A + B + C = 180^\circ\), so \(C = 90^\circ\).
By Sine rule, \(\dfrac{a}{\sin A} = \dfrac{b}{\sin B} = \dfrac{c}{\sin C}\).
\(\therefore \dfrac{a}{\sin 30^\circ} = \dfrac{b}{\sin 60^\circ} = \dfrac{c}{\sin 90^\circ}\), i.e. \(\dfrac{a}{\tfrac{1}{2}} = \dfrac{b}{\tfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}} = \dfrac{c}{1}\).
\(\therefore a : b : c = \dfrac{1}{2} : \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2} : 1 = 1 : \sqrt{3} : 2\).

subtopic: Solution of Triangle — Sine, Cosine and Projection Rules
stem: In \(\triangle ABC\), if \(a = 2\), \(b = 3\) and \(\sin A = \dfrac{2}{3}\) then find \(B\).
solution:
By sine rule, \(\dfrac{a}{\sin A} = \dfrac{b}{\sin B}\).
\(\therefore \dfrac{2}{\tfrac{2}{3}} = \dfrac{3}{\sin B}\), which gives \(\sin B = 1\).
\(\therefore B = 90^\circ = \dfrac{\pi}{2}\).

subtopic: Solution of Triangle — Sine, Cosine and Projection Rules
stem: In \(\triangle ABC\), prove that \(a(\sin B - \sin C) + b(\sin C - \sin A) + c(\sin A - \sin B) = 0\).
solution:
L.H.S. \(= a(\sin B - \sin C) + b(\sin C - \sin A) + c(\sin A - \sin B)\)
\(= a\sin B - a\sin C + b\sin C - b\sin A + c\sin A - c\sin B\)
\(= (a\sin B - b\sin A) + (b\sin C - c\sin B) + (c\sin A - a\sin C)\).
By the sine rule each bracket is zero (\(a\sin B = b\sin A\), \(b\sin C = c\sin B\), \(c\sin A = a\sin C\)).
\(= 0 + 0 + 0 = 0 = \) R.H.S.

subtopic: Solution of Triangle — Sine, Cosine and Projection Rules
stem: In \(\triangle ABC\), prove that \((a - b)\sin C + (b - c)\sin A + (c - a)\sin B = 0\).
solution:
L.H.S. \(= (a - b)\sin C + (b - c)\sin A + (c - a)\sin B\)
\(= (a\sin C - b\sin C) + (b\sin A - c\sin A) + (c\sin B - a\sin B)\)
\(= (a\sin C - c\sin A) + (b\sin A - a\sin B) + (c\sin B - b\sin C)\).
By the sine rule each bracket is zero.
\(= 0 + 0 + 0 = 0 = \) R.H.S.

subtopic: Solution of Triangle — Sine, Cosine and Projection Rules
stem: In \(\triangle ABC\), if \(a = 2\), \(b = 3\), \(c = 4\) then prove that the triangle is obtuse angled.
solution:
We know that the angle opposite to the largest side of a triangle is the largest angle of the triangle.
Here side \(AB\) (\(= c\)) is the largest side, so \(C\) is the largest angle. We show \(C\) is obtuse.
\(\cos C = \dfrac{a^2 + b^2 - c^2}{2ab} = \dfrac{2^2 + 3^2 - 4^2}{2(3)(4)} = \dfrac{-3}{24} = -\dfrac{1}{8}\).
As \(\cos C\) is negative, \(C\) is an obtuse angle.
\(\therefore \triangle ABC\) is an obtuse angled triangle.

subtopic: Solution of Triangle — Sine, Cosine and Projection Rules
stem: In \(\triangle ABC\), if \(A = 60^\circ\), \(b = 3\) and \(c = 8\) then find \(a\). Also find the circumradius of the triangle.
solution:
By Cosine rule, \(a^2 = b^2 + c^2 - 2bc\cos A\).
\(a^2 = 3^2 + 8^2 - 2(3)(8)\cos 60^\circ = 9 + 64 - 48 \times \dfrac{1}{2} = 73 - 24 = 49\).
\(\therefore a = 7\).
Now by sine rule \(\dfrac{a}{\sin A} = 2R\), so \(\dfrac{7}{\sin 60^\circ} = 2R\), i.e. \(\dfrac{7}{\tfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}} = 2R\).
\(\therefore R = \dfrac{7}{\sqrt{3}} = \dfrac{7\sqrt{3}}{3}\).
The circumradius of \(\triangle ABC\) is \(\dfrac{7\sqrt{3}}{3}\).

solution:
L.H.S. \(= (a + b)\cos C + (b + c)\cos A + (c + a)\cos B\)
\(= (a\cos C + b\cos C) + (b\cos A + c\cos A) + (c\cos B + a\cos B)\)
\(= (a\cos C + c\cos A) + (b\cos A + a\cos B) + (c\cos B + b\cos C)\).
By the projection rule, \(a\cos C + c\cos A = b\), \(b\cos A + a\cos B = c\), \(c\cos B + b\cos C = a\).
\(= a + b + c = \) R.H.S.

subtopic: Solution of Triangle — Sine, Cosine and Projection Rules
stem: In \(\triangle ABC\), prove that \(a(\cos C - \cos B) = 2(b - c)\cos^2\left(\dfrac{A}{2}\right)\).
solution:
By Projection rule, \(a\cos C + c\cos A = b\) and \(a\cos B + b\cos A = c\).
\(\therefore a\cos C = b - c\cos A\) and \(a\cos B = c - b\cos A\).
L.H.S. \(= a(\cos C - \cos B) = a\cos C - a\cos B\)
\(= (b - c\cos A) - (c - b\cos A)\)
\(= b - c\cos A - c + b\cos A\)
\(= (b - c) + (b - c)\cos A\)
\(= (b - c)(1 + \cos A)\)
\(= (b - c) \times 2\cos^2\dfrac{A}{2}\)
\(= 2(b - c)\cos^2\dfrac{A}{2} = \) R.H.S.

subtopic: Solution of Triangle — Sine, Cosine and Projection Rules
stem: Prove the Cosine rule using the Projection rule.
solution:
Given: In \(\triangle ABC\), \(a = b\cos C + c\cos B\), \(b = c\cos A + a\cos C\), \(c = a\cos B + b\cos A\).
Multiply these equations by \(a, b, c\) respectively:
\(a^2 = ab\cos C + ac\cos B\)
\(b^2 = bc\cos A + ab\cos C\)
\(c^2 = ac\cos B + bc\cos A\).
\(a^2 + b^2 - c^2 = (ab\cos C + ac\cos B) + (bc\cos A + ab\cos C) - (ac\cos B + bc\cos A)\)
\(= ab\cos C + ac\cos B + bc\cos A + ab\cos C - ac\cos B - bc\cos A\)
\(= 2ab\cos C\).
\(\therefore a^2 + b^2 - c^2 = 2ab\cos C\), i.e. \(c^2 = a^2 + b^2 - 2ab\cos C\).
Similarly we can prove that \(a^2 = b^2 + c^2 - 2bc\cos A\) and \(b^2 = c^2 + a^2 - 2ca\cos B\).

stem: In \(\triangle ABC\), if \(a = 13\), \(b = 14\), \(c = 15\) then find the values of (i) \(\cos A\) (ii) \(\sin\dfrac{A}{2}\) (iii) \(\cos\dfrac{A}{2}\) (iv) \(\tan\dfrac{A}{2}\) (v) \(A(\triangle ABC)\) (vi) \(\sin A\).
solution:
\(s = \dfrac{a + b + c}{2} = \dfrac{13 + 14 + 15}{2} = 21\).
\((s - a) = 21 - 13 = 8\), \((s - b) = 21 - 14 = 7\), \((s - c) = 21 - 15 = 6\).
(i) \(\cos A = \dfrac{b^2 + c^2 - a^2}{2bc} = \dfrac{13^2 + 15^2 - 14^2}{2(13)(15)} = \dfrac{198}{390} = \dfrac{33}{65}\).
(ii) \(\sin\dfrac{A}{2} = \sqrt{\dfrac{(s-b)(s-c)}{bc}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{7 \times 6}{14 \times 15}} = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{5}}\).
(iii) \(\cos\dfrac{A}{2} = \sqrt{\dfrac{s(s-a)}{bc}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{21 \times 8}{14 \times 15}} = \dfrac{2}{\sqrt{5}}\).
(iv) \(\tan\dfrac{A}{2} = \dfrac{\sin\tfrac{A}{2}}{\cos\tfrac{A}{2}} = \dfrac{1/\sqrt{5}}{2/\sqrt{5}} = \dfrac{1}{2}\).
(v) \(A(\triangle ABC) = \sqrt{s(s-a)(s-b)(s-c)} = \sqrt{21 \times 8 \times 7 \times 6} = 84\) sq. unit.
(vi) \(\sin A = 2\sin\dfrac{A}{2}\cos\dfrac{A}{2} = 2 \times \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{5}} \times \dfrac{2}{\sqrt{5}} = \dfrac{4}{5}\).

subtopic: Applications of Sine, Cosine and Projection Rules
stem: In \(\triangle ABC\), prove that \(\cot\dfrac{A}{2} + \cot\dfrac{B}{2} + \cot\dfrac{C}{2} = \dfrac{a + b + c}{b + c - a}\cot\dfrac{A}{2}\).
solution:
L.H.S. \(= \cot\dfrac{A}{2} + \cot\dfrac{B}{2} + \cot\dfrac{C}{2} = \dfrac{1}{\tan\tfrac{A}{2}} + \dfrac{1}{\tan\tfrac{B}{2}} + \dfrac{1}{\tan\tfrac{C}{2}}\).
Using \(\tan\dfrac{A}{2} = \sqrt{\dfrac{(s-b)(s-c)}{s(s-a)}}\) and similarly for \(B, C\),
\(= \sqrt{\dfrac{s(s-a)}{(s-b)(s-c)}} + \sqrt{\dfrac{s(s-b)}{(s-a)(s-c)}} + \sqrt{\dfrac{s(s-c)}{(s-a)(s-b)}}\)
\(= \sqrt{\dfrac{s(s-a)^2}{(s-b)(s-c)(s-a)}} + \sqrt{\dfrac{s(s-b)^2}{(s-a)(s-c)(s-b)}} + \sqrt{\dfrac{s(s-c)^2}{(s-b)(s-a)(s-c)}}\)
\(= \sqrt{\dfrac{s}{(s-b)(s-a)(s-c)}}\,\{(s-a) + (s-b) + (s-c)\}\)
\(= \sqrt{\dfrac{s}{(s-b)(s-a)(s-c)}}\,\{3s - (a + b + c)\}\)
\(= \sqrt{\dfrac{s}{(s-b)(s-a)(s-c)}}\,\{3s - 2s\}\)
\(= \sqrt{\dfrac{s}{(s-b)(s-a)(s-c)}} \times s\)
\(= \dfrac{2s}{2s - 2a}\sqrt{\dfrac{s(s-a)}{(s-b)(s-c)}}\)
\(= \dfrac{a + b + c}{a + b + c - 2a}\sqrt{\dfrac{s(s-a)}{(s-b)(s-c)}}\)
\(= \dfrac{a + b + c}{b + c - a}\cot\dfrac{A}{2} = \) R.H.S.

context: Find the principal values of the following :
solution:
We have \(\sin\left(-\frac{\pi}{6}\right) = -\frac{1}{2}\), where \(-\frac{1}{2} \in [-1,1]\) and \(-\frac{\pi}{6} \in \left[-\frac{\pi}{2},\frac{\pi}{2}\right]\).
\(\therefore \sin^{-1}\left(-\frac{1}{2}\right) = -\frac{\pi}{6}\).
The principal value of \(\sin^{-1}\left(-\frac{1}{2}\right)\) is \(-\frac{\pi}{6}\).

subtopic: Inverse Trigonometric Functions and Principal Values
context: Find the principal values of the following :
solution:
We have \(\cos\frac{\pi}{6} = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\), where \(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} \in [-1,1]\) and \(\frac{\pi}{6} \in [0,\pi]\).
\(\cos^{-1}\left(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right) = \frac{\pi}{6}\).
The principal value of \(\cos^{-1}\left(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right)\) is \(\frac{\pi}{6}\).

context: Find the principal values of the following :
solution:

\(\therefore\) The principal value of \(\cot^{-1}\left(-\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\right)\) is \(\frac{2\pi}{3}\).

context: Find the values of the following :
solution:
\(\sin^{-1}\left(\sin\frac{5\pi}{3}\right) = \sin^{-1}\left(\sin\left(2\pi-\frac{\pi}{3}\right)\right) = \sin^{-1}\left(\sin\left(-\frac{\pi}{3}\right)\right) = -\frac{\pi}{3}\), as \(-\frac{\pi}{3} \in \left[-\frac{\pi}{2},\frac{\pi}{2}\right]\).
\(\therefore \sin^{-1}\left(\sin\frac{5\pi}{3}\right) = -\frac{\pi}{3}\).

context: Find the values of the following :

context: Find the values of the following :
solution:
We have \(\cos^{-1}(-x) = \pi - \cos^{-1}x\).
\(\therefore \sin\left(\cos^{-1}\left(-\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\right)\right) = \sin\left(\pi - \cos^{-1}\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\right) = \sin\left(\pi - \frac{\pi}{4}\right) = \sin\left(\frac{3\pi}{4}\right) = \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\).
\(\therefore \sin\left(\cos^{-1}\left(-\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\right)\right) = \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\).

context: Find the values of the following :
solution:
Let \(\cos^{-1}\frac{4}{5} = \theta\) and \(\tan^{-1}\frac{5}{12} = \phi\).
\(\therefore \cos\theta = \frac{4}{5}\) and \(\tan\phi = \frac{5}{12}\).
\(\therefore \sin\theta = \frac{3}{5}\) and \(\sin\phi = \frac{5}{13}\), \(\cos\phi = \frac{12}{13}\).
\(\sin\left(\cos^{-1}\frac{4}{5} + \tan^{-1}\frac{5}{12}\right) = \sin(\theta+\phi) = \sin\theta\cos\phi + \cos\theta\sin\phi = \frac{3}{5}\cdot\frac{12}{13} + \frac{4}{5}\cdot\frac{5}{13} = \frac{56}{65}\).
\(\therefore \sin\left(\cos^{-1}\frac{4}{5} + \tan^{-1}\frac{5}{12}\right) = \frac{56}{65}\).

context: Find the values of the following :
solution:
We have, if \(-1 \le x \le 1\) then \(\sin^{-1}x + \cos^{-1}x = \frac{\pi}{2}\).
Here \(-1 < \frac{3}{5} < 1\).
\(\therefore \sin^{-1}\left(\frac{3}{5}\right) + \cos^{-1}\left(\frac{3}{5}\right) = \frac{\pi}{2}\).
\(\therefore \sin\left[\sin^{-1}\left(\frac{3}{5}\right) + \cos^{-1}\left(\frac{3}{5}\right)\right] = \sin\left(\frac{\pi}{2}\right) = 1\).

context: Find the values of the following :
solution:
\(\cos^{-1}\left(-\frac{1}{2}\right) = \frac{2\pi}{3}\) and \(\tan^{-1}\sqrt{3} = \frac{\pi}{3}\).
\(\therefore \cos\left[\cos^{-1}\left(-\frac{1}{2}\right) + \tan^{-1}\sqrt{3}\right] = \cos\left(\frac{2\pi}{3} + \frac{\pi}{3}\right) = \cos\pi = -1\).

We have for \(|x| \le 1\), \(\sin^{-1}x + \cos^{-1}x = \frac{\pi}{2}\).
\(\therefore \cos^{-1}x = \frac{\pi}{2} - \sin^{-1}x\).
Now using \(\sin\left(\frac{\pi}{2} - \theta\right) = \cos\theta\),
\(\sin(\cos^{-1}x) = \sin\left(\frac{\pi}{2} - \sin^{-1}x\right) = \cos(\sin^{-1}x)\).
\(\therefore \sin(\cos^{-1}x) = \cos(\sin^{-1}x)\).

context: Prove the following :
solution:
[Note: the printed stem shows \(-\frac{1}{3}\); the book's solution proves the result using \(\frac{1}{3}\).]
\(2\tan^{-1}\frac{1}{3} = \tan^{-1}\frac{1}{3} + \tan^{-1}\frac{1}{3}\), as \(xy = \frac{1}{3}\times\frac{1}{3} = \frac{1}{9} < 1\)
\(= \tan^{-1}\left(\frac{\frac{1}{3}+\frac{1}{3}}{1 - \frac{1}{3}\cdot\frac{1}{3}}\right) = \tan^{-1}\frac{3}{4} = \theta\) (say).
\(\therefore \tan\theta = \frac{3}{4}\), \(0 < \theta < \frac{\pi}{2}\).
\(\therefore \sin\theta = \frac{3}{5}\), \(\therefore \theta = \sin^{-1}\frac{3}{5}\).
\(\therefore 2\tan^{-1}\frac{1}{3} = \tan^{-1}\frac{3}{4} = \sin^{-1}\frac{3}{5}\).
\(\therefore 2\tan^{-1}\frac{1}{3} + \cos^{-1}\frac{3}{5} = \sin^{-1}\frac{3}{5} + \cos^{-1}\frac{3}{5} = \frac{\pi}{2}\).

context: Prove the following :

solution:
We use the result: \(\tan^{-1}x + \tan^{-1}y = \pi + \tan^{-1}\left(\frac{x+y}{1-xy}\right)\) if \(xy > 1\).
Here \(xy = 1 \times 2 = 2 > 1\).
\(\therefore \tan^{-1}1 + \tan^{-1}2 = \pi + \tan^{-1}\left(\frac{1+2}{1-(1)(2)}\right) = \pi + \tan^{-1}\left(\frac{3}{1-2}\right) = \pi + \tan^{-1}(-3) = \pi - \tan^{-1}3\) (As \(\tan^{-1}(-x) = -\tan^{-1}x\)).
\(\therefore \tan^{-1}1 + \tan^{-1}2 + \tan^{-1}3 = \pi\).

Let \(\cos^{-1}\frac{4}{5} = \theta\). Then \(0 < \theta < \frac{\pi}{2}\) and \(\cos\theta = \frac{4}{5}\).
\(\therefore \sin\theta = \frac{3}{5}\).
Let \(\cos^{-1}\frac{12}{13} = \phi\). Then \(0 < \phi < \frac{\pi}{2}\) and \(\cos\phi = \frac{12}{13}\).
\(\sin\phi = \frac{5}{13}\).
\(\cos(\theta+\phi) = \cos\theta\cos\phi - \sin\theta\sin\phi = \left(\frac{4}{5}\right)\left(\frac{12}{13}\right) - \left(\frac{3}{5}\right)\left(\frac{5}{13}\right) = \frac{48}{65} - \frac{15}{65} = \frac{33}{65}\).
\(\therefore \cos(\theta+\phi) = \frac{33}{65}\) ...(1)
Also \(0 < \theta < \frac{\pi}{2}\) and \(0 < \phi < \frac{\pi}{2}\).
\(\therefore 0 < \theta+\phi < \pi\).
\(\therefore\) from (1), \(\theta+\phi = \cos^{-1}\frac{33}{65}\).
\(\therefore \cos^{-1}\frac{4}{5} + \cos^{-1}\frac{12}{13} = \cos^{-1}\frac{33}{65}\).

stem: The principal solutions of the equation \(\sin\theta = \dfrac{-1}{2}\) are ______.
solution: \(\sin\theta=-\tfrac12\) is negative, so \(\theta\) lies in the third and fourth quadrants in \([0,2\pi)\): \(\theta=\pi+\tfrac{\pi}{6}=\tfrac{7\pi}{6}\) and \(\theta=2\pi-\tfrac{\pi}{6}=\tfrac{11\pi}{6}\).

stem: The principal solutions of the equation \(\cot\theta = \sqrt{3}\) are ______.
solution: \(\cot\theta=\sqrt3\Rightarrow\tan\theta=\tfrac{1}{\sqrt3}\), positive, so \(\theta\) is in the first and third quadrants: \(\theta=\tfrac{\pi}{6}\) and \(\theta=\pi+\tfrac{\pi}{6}=\tfrac{7\pi}{6}\).

stem: The general solution of \(\sec x = \sqrt{2}\) is ______.
solution: \(\sec x=\sqrt2\Rightarrow\cos x=\tfrac{1}{\sqrt2}=\cos\tfrac{\pi}{4}\), so \(x=2n\pi\pm\tfrac{\pi}{4}\).

stem: If \(\cos p\theta = \cos q\theta,\ p \neq q\) then ______.
solution: \(\cos p\theta=\cos q\theta\Rightarrow p\theta=2n\pi\pm q\theta\Rightarrow(p\mp q)\theta=2n\pi\Rightarrow\theta=\tfrac{2n\pi}{p\pm q}\).

stem: If the polar co-ordinates of a point are \(\left(2, \dfrac{\pi}{4}\right)\) then its cartesian co-ordinates are ______.
solution: \(x=r\cos\theta=2\cos\tfrac{\pi}{4}=\sqrt2\), \(y=r\sin\theta=2\sin\tfrac{\pi}{4}=\sqrt2\).

stem: If \(\sqrt{3}\cos x - \sin x = 1\), then the general value of \(x\) is ______.
solution: Divide by \(2\): \(\tfrac{\sqrt3}{2}\cos x-\tfrac12\sin x=\tfrac12\Rightarrow\cos\!\left(x+\tfrac{\pi}{6}\right)=\tfrac12=\cos\tfrac{\pi}{3}\Rightarrow x+\tfrac{\pi}{6}=2n\pi\pm\tfrac{\pi}{3}\Rightarrow x=2n\pi\pm\tfrac{\pi}{3}-\tfrac{\pi}{6}\).

stem: If \(\tan\theta + \tan 2\theta + \tan 3\theta = \tan\theta\,\tan 2\theta\,\tan 3\theta\), then the general value of \(\theta\) is ______.
solution:
[Textbook defect: the complete solution set is \(\theta=\dfrac{n\pi}{3}\), which is not among the four printed alternatives. The official key marks \(\dfrac{n\pi}{6}\), retained here to match the board: it contains the whole solution set as its even-\(n\) members, but also contains values such as \(\theta=\dfrac{\pi}{6}\) at which \(\tan 3\theta\) is undefined.]

Since \(3\theta=\theta+2\theta\), \(\tan 3\theta=\dfrac{\tan\theta+\tan 2\theta}{1-\tan\theta\tan 2\theta}\), that is \(\tan\theta+\tan 2\theta=\tan 3\theta\left(1-\tan\theta\tan 2\theta\right)\).

Substituting this in the given equation:

\(\tan 3\theta\left(1-\tan\theta\tan 2\theta\right)+\tan 3\theta=\tan\theta\tan 2\theta\tan 3\theta\)

\(\Rightarrow\ 2\tan 3\theta\left(1-\tan\theta\tan 2\theta\right)=0\).

The factor \(1-\tan\theta\tan 2\theta\) vanishes exactly where \(\tan 3\theta\) is undefined, so it yields no solution of the given equation. Hence \(\tan 3\theta=0\), i.e. \(3\theta=n\pi\), giving \(\theta=\dfrac{n\pi}{3}\).

Following the official key, (B).
